title: Elastic wave in a bar from a pressure step (explicit)
source: d'Alembert's solution of the one-dimensional wave equation: c = √(E/ρ), particle velocity v = p/(ρc); Graff, Wave Motion in Elastic Solids, Dover 1991, §2.1

quantities.quantity: displacement of the loaded end at t = 0.06
quantities.reason: the end moves at the particle velocity p/(ρc) from the start; the discrete wave's ringing behind the front changes the end's displacement by well under 1%

quantities.quantity: particle velocity at x = 5, 20 elements behind the front, at t = 0.06
quantities.reason: central differences ring behind a step front (dispersion); bulk viscosity damps it within a few elements, leaving about 1% twenty elements behind
external work = kinetic + internal + dissipated energy; the solver warns above 1%
